primary.root_cause: The APB FSM does not support reading from SRAM addresses > 5, forcing prdata to 0 and asserting pslverr for any out-of-range access.
primary.proposed_fix: Extend the APB read case statement to handle addresses > 5 by mapping them to sram_mem[paddr]. Clear pslverr for valid memory accesses and drive prdata with the corresponding SRAM byte.

alternative.root_cause: The SRAM write logic ignores the specified sram_valid trigger and writes continuously whenever r_Enable is 2, while sram_valid is incorrectly declared as an output port instead of an input.
evidence: always @(posedge pclk) begin if (r_Enable == 2'b11) begin sram_mem[r_write_address[7:0]] <= r_write_data; end end
sram_valid: At positive edge of this signal, data in r_write_data is latched to address in r_write_address.
alternative.proposed_fix: Change sram_valid to an input port and use it as a clock enable for the SRAM write logic. Remove the continuous write condition tied to r_Enable.
